question: What has Raymond James said about its affiliation models, and has the mix shifted?

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®.

Raymond James Financial: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with Raymond James directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs) and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
Raymond James Financial: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, and serve predominantly retail clients.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its AdvisorChoice affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its affiliation spectrum as spanning Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, noting that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.

Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors; they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

Raymond James Financial: Through its domestic RCS division, Raymond James offers third-party RIAs and broker-dealers custodial services, trade execution, research and other support; financial advisors associated with RCS firms are not included in Raymond James' advisor counts.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, offering all the affiliation options and therefore the largest addressable market in the industry.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody—with critical mass and decades of experience in each, and that it is not a new venture for the firm.

Raymond James Financial: On the affiliation mix, CEO Paul Reilly said RCS has by far the highest percentage growth, while this year the employee channel led the way; he expected some improvement in the independent contractor model.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, while still seeing success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option.
Raymond James Financial: Recruiting activity is broad-based across affiliation options but has been more heavily tilted toward the independent contractor side in the last six months.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James is seeing a good uptick in the employee affiliation option, and describes the mix shift as relating to the comp ratio because of the payout difference between the independent and employee channels.

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation options differ in how advisors spend their time day-to-day: the employee option suits those focused on building their books of business, while others want to run a business including building a team, paying benefits, and dealing with real estate and legal aspects.

Raymond James Financial: Recruiting success is spread across all affiliation channels; the independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in dollar volume, while the RIA custody division is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states it has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates, wanting advisors to fall in love with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its multiple affiliation options collectively as AdvisorChoice, offered to financial advisors who primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

Raymond James Financial: Through AdvisorChoice, Raymond James says advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its best of both worlds value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which it says resonates with advisors across all its affiliation options.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James lists its value proposition pillars as a service-first culture, respect for financial advisor independence, and a comprehensive and growing product and solution set.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says its affiliation strategy lets advisors not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says its independent contractor advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of its support as they determine they need.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its mission for the affiliation models as to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals, tied to multiple affiliation options, best of both worlds, advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states it competes directly with national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from newer entrants including fintechs, as well as indirect competition for investment assets from insurance companies, real estate firms and hedge funds.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says the continued industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs some of which are backed by private equity investors, has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says many of its competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or less, many compete with the largest check, and many change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James names PE-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic, saying they have been extremely aggressive in paying higher and higher multiples for advisors over the last three years.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it still sees pressure on the existing advisor base from private equity roll-ups, which in the absence of a value proposition compete with big checks.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says many competitors that focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest only a fraction of what it does in technology, making it hard for them to remain competitive.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says competitors that lack a true differentiated value proposition lead with the highest check.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says advisors are coming to it from a lot of different competitor firms, including wirehouses, regionals and other independents.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says private equity has certainly been competitive over the last five years, as well as some of the strategic firms.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James notes it is possible that certain of its competitors will withdraw from the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when they affiliate with a new firm.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 3,693 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 5,019 independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 3,826 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2024.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 4,961 independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2024.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 3,878 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported 5,065 independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $332 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its employee affiliation model as of March 31, 2020.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $318 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its independent contractor affiliation model as of March 31, 2020.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $46 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its RIA & Custody Services (RCS) affiliation model as of March 31, 2020.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $631 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its employee affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $543 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its independent contractor affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported $186 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its RIA & Custody Services (RCS) affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported AUA associated with firms in its RCS division totaled $217.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $224.6 billion as of December 31, 2025.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $228.2 billion as of March 31, 2026.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James reported PCG AUA associated with RCS firms of $251.3 billion as of June 30, 2026.

Raymond James Financial: Paul Shoukry stated that over the last year much more of Raymond James's recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, indicating a mix shift toward independent.

Raymond James Financial: Paul Reilly stated that RCS is by far the highest percentage growth, and in total dollars the employee channel led the way this fiscal year (2024), whereas a couple of years ago it was the independent channel.

Raymond James Financial: Whether the mix across Raymond James affiliation models has shifted over time can be reported on this evidence, but only descriptively from management and trade-press statements rather than from one continuous series: the headcount and AUA figures in the matrix sit on different bases and different periods (whole-firm headcount at September 30 of 2023–2025; affiliation-model AUA at March 31 of 2020 and 2025; RCS-division AUA at various quarter-ends from 2025 to 2026), so they are not comparable as a single mix series. Management's own statements (RJF-TR-2024Q3#66, RJF-TR-2026Q1#44, RJF-TR-2026Q1#46, RJF-TRADE-2026-10-29-WM-01#0) do describe shifts over time and are cited under aspect a6.
